title: Frugality Is Hard to Afford
design_notes: Nielsen Consumer Panel (2006-2014, about 104,000 households, toilet paper, paper towels, laundry detergent, cigarettes). DiD compares low-income vs. higher-income households between the first week of the month (high liquidity) and the rest of the month, with household fixed effects; the 'treatment' is a recurring calendar-position indicator, not a one-time adoption. Includes IV-style robustness (liquidity instrument) and category-specific outcomes (bulk buying, purchase acceleration).
eligible_reason: Treatment is a recurring within-month timing indicator interacted with income group, not a binary treatment switching on at unit-specific dates; no staggered adoption.
screener_notes: Licensed Nielsen Consumer Panel data via the Kilts Center (cannot be redistributed); no package in batch. Ineligible on design.
screened_from: article text only (no package_dir or regressions file in batch_t2_004)
